project.name: task-planner
project.description: A hierarchical task planner (Year -> Month -> Week -> Day) with project-based weekly planning, deadline tracking, and animated progress bars, deployed on Cloudflare's free plan with Supabase as the backend.

constraints: Stay within Cloudflare Pages free tier: 500 builds/month, unlimited static requests.
If using Cloudflare Workers for API routes, stay within 100,000 requests/day free tier limit.
Avoid Durable Objects / paid-only Cloudflare features.
Do not rely on Cloudflare KV/D1 for primary data storage — Supabase is the system of record.
Keep bundle size small; prefer edge-friendly frameworks (e.g. Astro, SvelteKit, Next.js on Pages, or plain Vite + React).

usage: Postgres database for all planning data (years, months, weeks, projects, tasks, subtasks, sub-subtasks).
Supabase Auth for user login (email/password or magic link).
Row Level Security (RLS) enabled on all tables, scoped to auth.uid().
Supabase client SDK called directly from the frontend where possible to avoid needing a custom backend server (keeps Cloudflare usage minimal).

deep_navy.usage: Primary brand color. Header background, primary buttons, active nav state, dark text on light surfaces.

indigo.usage: Secondary accent. Hover/active states, progress bar fill (mid-tone), project markers, focus rings.

sky_blue.usage: Interactive accent. Links, '<' '>' navigation buttons, add-project button, badges, progress bar highlight.

pale_aqua.usage: Background / surface tint. Card backgrounds, hover backgrounds, dividers, disabled states, subtle fills.

notes: Use deep_navy + white text for header for strong contrast.
Use pale_aqua as the main app background (very light tint, e.g. mixed with white) so cards in indigo/sky_blue pop.
Progress bar fill can use a gradient from sky_blue to indigo as it fills, sitting on a pale_aqua track.
Ensure WCAG AA contrast for all text/background combinations; do not rely on color alone to signal task completion (also use checkmarks/strikethrough).

design_system.typography: Clean sans-serif (e.g. Inter or system-ui). Clear size hierarchy: Year/Month labels largest, project titles medium, task/subtask text smaller.
design_system.spacing: Card-based layout with generous padding, rounded corners (8-12px), soft shadows for project cards.

information_architecture.hierarchy: Yearly Plan -> Monthly Plan -> Weekly Plan -> Daily Plan

yearly_plan.scope: Current year only (no multi-year switch required in v1).
yearly_plan.purpose: High-level overview: shows months as tiles, each summarizing completion stats for that month.

monthly_plan.purpose: Shows the weeks within the selected month as tiles/rows, each summarizing that week's completion stats.

weekly_plan.purpose: THE CORE / DEFAULT VIEW of the app. Shows projects and their tasks laid out across the 7 days of the week (Monday start).
weekly_plan.navigates_to: daily_plan (implicit, via day columns within the week view)

daily_plan.purpose: Within a week, each day column shows that day's tasks. Users can drill into a single day for a focused view if desired, but the primary interaction happens inline within the weekly view.
daily_plan.implementation_note: Daily plan can be either (a) an inline column within weekly_plan, or (b) an optional expanded/focused single-day view triggered by clicking a day header. Implement (a) as the default and (b) as a stretch enhancement.

items.label: Plans
items.description: Opens the planning hierarchy: Yearly / Monthly / Weekly (default) view switcher.
items.behavior: Clicking 'Plans' returns user to the last-viewed planning level, defaulting to Weekly.

items.label: Stats
items.description: Opens a stats/analytics view: completion rates over time, per-project progress, streaks, etc.
items.behavior: Separate page/route showing aggregated charts (e.g. tasks completed per week, per month, per project).

week_navigator.position: Directly below header, right-aligned, sitting above the main weekly planning area.

components.action: Navigate to the previous week (week_offset - 1). Loads that week's projects/tasks from Supabase.

components.description: Shows the currently viewed week, e.g. 'Sep 8 - Sep 14, 2026'. Optionally shows 'This Week' badge when offset = 0.
components.position: between prev and next buttons, or just left of them

components.action: Navigate to the next week (week_offset + 1). Loads that week's projects/tasks from Supabase.

behavior_notes: Navigation must work for both past weeks (view/edit historical tasks) and future weeks (plan ahead).
Preserve scroll position / avoid layout shift when switching weeks.
Disable or visually de-emphasize navigation only if there's a hard bound (v1: no hard bound, allow unlimited past/future navigation).

week_progress_bar.position: Directly below the week navigator, above the main weekly planning grid.

calculation.definition_of_task: Counts top-level project tasks scheduled within the current week (see data_model.tasks). Whether subtasks/sub-subtasks also count toward this ratio is configurable (default: only top-level tasks count, to keep the math simple and predictable).
calculation.example: A week with 1 total task fills 100% when that 1 task is completed. A week with 3 total tasks fills 33.3% per completed task, reaching 100% only when all 3 are completed.
calculation.edge_case_zero_tasks: If a week has 0 tasks, show the bar empty (0%) and optionally display 'No tasks planned this week' instead of a percentage.

animation.trigger: Fires whenever a task's completed state changes, or when switching weeks (bar animates from 0 to the target fill on load).
animation.style: CSS transition on width (or transform: scaleX) over ~400-600ms with an ease-out curve.
animation.micro_interaction: On reaching 100%, play a subtle celebratory pulse/glow animation using the palette (e.g. brief glow in #4382DF).

week_progress_bar.display: Show the percentage or 'x / y tasks' label near the bar.

weekly_main_planning_area.position: Below the progress bar; this is the primary content area of the app.
weekly_main_planning_area.structure: A board of Projects, each project expandable to show its Tasks distributed across the 7 day-columns of the current week (Mon-Sun).

add_project.label: + Add Project
add_project.color: #4382DF on white, or filled #112E81 button with white text
add_project.action: Opens a form/modal to create a new project: name, optional description, optional deadline (date picker), optional color tag.
add_project.position: Top of the weekly planning area, above or alongside the project list.

fields_shown: deadline (if set, with countdown or overdue indicator)
progress (tasks completed / total tasks for this project within the week, or overall)

deadline_display.overdue: Highlight in a warning tone (e.g. red/orange accent, kept distinct from the 4-color brand palette for clarity as a status color) if deadline has passed and project isn't complete.
deadline_display.upcoming: Show days remaining, e.g. 'Due in 3 days'.

task_layout_within_project.structure: Each project displays a 7-column (Mon-Sun) mini-grid or a day-grouped list. Tasks are assigned to a specific day of the current week.
task_layout_within_project.add_task: Each day column within a project has an 'add task' affordance (small plus icon) to create a task for that project on that specific day.
task_layout_within_project.task_completion_effect: Toggling a task's checkbox updates the week_progress_bar calculation in real time (optimistic UI update, then persist to Supabase).

subtask_layout.description: Each task (already scoped to a specific day) can be expanded to reveal sub-tasks, further breaking down the work for that day.
subtask_layout.add_subtask: Plus button within an expanded task row: 'add sub-task'.
subtask_layout.nesting_note: Sub-tasks belong to a single day (inherited from their parent task's day) — they do not get independently reassigned to a different day.

sub_subtask_layout.description: Each sub-task can itself be expanded to add sub-sub-tasks — a third level of granularity for the project task on that day.
sub_subtask_layout.add_sub_subtask: Plus button within an expanded sub-task row: 'add sub-sub-task'.
sub_subtask_layout.depth_limit: v1 supports exactly 3 levels: Task -> Sub-task -> Sub-sub-task. Do not implement unlimited recursive nesting; hardcode 3 levels for simplicity and UI clarity.

data_model.notes: All tables include id (uuid, pk), user_id (uuid, fk to auth.users, RLS scoped), created_at, updated_at.

columns: day_date (date — the specific calendar day within the week this task is assigned to)
tasks.notes: day_date determines both which week AND which day column the task appears in. Week is derived from day_date (Mon-Sun range), not stored separately.

derived_views_or_queries: week_stats: given a Monday date, SUM(tasks WHERE day_date BETWEEN monday AND sunday), COUNT completed vs total -> feeds week_progress_bar.
month_stats: aggregate week_stats across all weeks overlapping the given month -> feeds monthly_plan tiles.
year_stats: aggregate month_stats across the current year -> feeds yearly_plan tiles.
project_stats: per-project completed/total across all its tasks (optionally scoped to current week or all-time) -> feeds project_card progress and the Stats page.
data_model.row_level_security: Enable RLS on all four tables; policy: user_id = auth.uid() for select/insert/update/delete.

pages_and_routes.note: weekStartDate is the Monday of the target week; drives the '<' '>' navigation.

interaction_and_animation_requirements: Progress bar fill animates smoothly on any task toggle and on week change (see week_progress_bar.animation).
Checking off a task gives immediate visual feedback (checkmark animation, strikethrough on title).
Adding a project/task/subtask/sub-subtask opens a lightweight modal or inline form — avoid full page reloads (SPA-style state updates).
Week navigation ('<' / '>') should transition content smoothly (e.g. slight fade or slide) rather than an abrupt re-render.
non_functional_requirements: Responsive design: usable on both desktop and mobile (the 7-day grid should collapse to a scrollable/stacked layout on narrow screens).
Optimistic UI updates with Supabase writes in the background; handle and surface errors gracefully (toast/snackbar).
Keep API/database calls minimal per view to respect Cloudflare Workers free-tier request limits — batch queries per week/month/year rather than per-task.
Accessible: keyboard navigable, proper ARIA labels on buttons like '<' '>' and add-project/add-task controls.
out_of_scope_for_v1: Team/multi-user collaboration on the same project (single-user data model for now).
